clue.text: Takes off cloaks, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for cloaks

parts.note: capes are sleeveless cloaks

explanation.surface: Someone removing cloaks, though not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' looks like undressing, matching the cloaks, but here it means mimics.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, and to ape is likewise to imitate.

clue.text: Battleground — one banked with heavy armour

parts.note: a river is something with banks on either side
plate armour is the heavy metal kind

explanation.surface: A battlefield where one side is dug in behind heavy armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the River Plate (1939) was a naval action off South America, so the battleground is water.
explanation.definitionFit: The estuary between Argentina and Uruguay was the scene of a famous 1939 naval battle.

parts.note: V is the victory sign made with two fingers

indicators.note: review suggests looking over again and rearranging the letters of the word before it

explanation.surface: A V-sign given at a battle site, under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' is the anagram signal, working on the word 'under' beside it; 'victory sign' is the two-finger V.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city was the site of the longest battle of the First World War, in 1916.

parts.note: read as a sports arena in the capital where football teams do battle, it is also the site of a real 1066 battle in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A London site where battles are fought.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea football club plays at this ground in London; the real battle of 1066 was fought near York.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea's stadium is a London sports ground and shares its name with a Yorkshire battle site of 1066.

clue.text: Battleground contains money from the South

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the south means read upwards, so the hidden letters run backwards
contains says the letters are held within the word battleground

explanation.surface: A battlefield found to contain money brought up from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' finds TLEG inside BATTLEGROUND; 'from the South' turns it upwards. Gelt is also a theme battle site in Cumbria (1570).
explanation.definitionFit: Gelt is a slang word for money, borrowed from Yiddish and German.

indicators.note: misled suggests the letters have been led astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A saboteur fooled a person using a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks machinery or plans, so is a wrecker.

definitions.meaning: a town in northern France, scene of a 1915 battle
lavatories, a British word for toilets

explanation.surface: Battleground facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Loos in France was a First World War battle site, and loos are British toilets.

clue.text: Fitting metal bearings in fresh cover

indicators.note: in puts the metal and bearings inside the word for fresh
cover says the word for fresh wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky means pert
tin is a metal
E and N, east and north, are compass bearings

explanation.surface: Fitting metal bearings into a new housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'cover' both signal the container: the word for fresh covers the metal and bearings. 'Fitting' looks like a workshop job but means appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent is relevant to the matter, that is apt or fitting.

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Time to sit and think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb, ponder, but is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Battleground discovered when South African crosses border

indicators.note: crosses suggests one piece spanning another, so the south and African pair goes around the border

parts.note: a Moor is a North African
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A battlefield found when a South African crosses a border.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDGEMOOR in Somerset saw the defeat of Monmouth's rebellion in 1685.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset moor was the site of the last pitched battle on English soil, in 1685.

clue.text: March into conflict with squadron leader after positional losses

parts.note: a march is a demo, a protest procession

indicators.note: conflict suggests the letters of into clash and fall into disorder
leader picks out the first letter of squadron

explanation.surface: Marching into battle with the squadron leader following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' is the anagram signal on 'into'; 'leader' takes the first letter of 'squadron'. 'March' looks like a verb but is a noun, a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotions are losses of rank, falls in one's position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Ignore alarm bells echoing in error

indicators.note: echoing points to a word repeated as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: making a mistake is slipping

explanation.surface: Ignoring warning bells, whose echoes ring out by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is to stay in bed past the time set, ignoring the alarm clock.

definitions.meaning: a French town where Prussia defeated France in 1870
a saloon car, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Battleground vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan in France was an 1870 battle site; a sedan is also a car or sedan chair.

indicators.note: wildly suggests the letters of sob run riot into a new order

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
ENE, east-north-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing wildly about the way things are going, appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges SOB to OBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to decency, repulsive or disgusting.

clue.text: Battleground stories about the king's men of Cork?

parts.note: the Somme is the river battlefield of 1916

indicators.note: about says the word for stories goes round the letter for king

parts.note: lies are false stories
R, for rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: Tales from a battlefield about the king's men of an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' looks like the Irish county, but the capital is only there to mislead: wine waiters draw corks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sommeliers are wine waiters, who handle bottles and their corks.

clue.text: Group of hygiene managers behind irrigation procedure

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some hygiene managers dealing with a rear irrigation procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes fluid into the rectum, an irrigation of the behind.

clue.text: Went ahead, returning thanks to foreign character

indicators.note: returning says the word for went ahead is read backwards

parts.note: led means went ahead, at the front
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone led the way, coming back to thank a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LED into DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character.

clue.text: Louis sends away for offensive material

parts.note: Lew is a short form of the name Louis

indicators.note: away suggests the letters of sends are sent off into a new order

explanation.surface: Louis dispatches obscene material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges SENDS to DNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewdness is crude sexual indecency, the stuff of offensive material.

definitions.meaning: a fish that swims in a school

explanation.surface: A trick played by one pupil at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means mock or hoax, and a cod is a fish found in schools.

indicators.note: introduced says the poem is brought into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a cull is a selective slaughter of animals
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A battlefield massacre, commemorated by a new poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Culloden in the Scottish Highlands saw the Jacobites' final defeat in 1746.

clue.text: Battleground near Moroccan capital in ruins

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the head of the word Moroccan
in ruins suggests the letters of near are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A battlefield near a Moroccan capital lying in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' is the anagram signal on 'near'; 'capital' takes the head letter of 'Moroccan'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French river Marne was the scene of two major battles of the First World War.

clue.text: Better conditions for naked swimmer announced

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken and heard as something else

parts.note: an unclothed eel would be a nude eel

explanation.surface: Better conditions declared for someone swimming in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Deal was Roosevelt's 1930s American recovery programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A new deal is a fresh, more favourable arrangement for people.

indicators.note: spread suggests treacle smeared about, its letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's tangled mess of treacle spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electra complex is the daughter's counterpart of the Oedipus complex.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis Electra names a girl's rivalry with her mother for her father.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flag that some people pay no attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show nationality.

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of battle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battlefield leading to an author being stuck for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battleground' looks like one word, the theme, but splits: BATTLE is ground up. 'writer's block' is a slab to write on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat slab of stone or wax on which people once wrote.

clue.text: Battleground tours designed to be shocking

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a 1914 battle

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of tours are arranged to a new plan

explanation.surface: Battlefield tours planned to appal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges TOURS to TROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstrous means outrageous or appalling, so shocking.

definitions.meaning: to slope or lean, like a ship pitching
an old word for a canvas awning or covering over a cart or stall

explanation.surface: Put up a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilt means pitch or slope, and a tilt is also a canvas awning.

clue.text: Setter's sad, having left out tint

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so setter's is I'M, I am

indicators.note: out says a letter is left out of the word for sad

parts.note: blue means sad

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is gloomy at being excluded from a tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left out' removes L from BLUE to leave BUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to dye or saturate with colour, so to tint.

indicators.note: said points to letters spoken rather than written

parts.note: the letter E twice, spoken as plural, is Es

explanation.surface: Letters read out to bring comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from pain or worry, a state of comfort.

indicators.note: first says the river comes ahead of the letter for large

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Ouse in England

explanation.surface: A bird picks the large bloom first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as a thing that flows: the Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel or ouzel is a thrush-like bird, such as the ring ouzel.

indicators.note: produce suggests the letters of green seas are made into something new

explanation.surface: Green seas making one thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst figuratively means eagerness, a keen desire for something.
